title: containerd trips over Dockerfile instruction VOLUME for Windows container image
body:
### Description

This bug report is an extract with my findings during the discussion with @participant2 in https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/6589#issuecomment-1428600140 which I'm copying/describing below:

I build a Windows container image based on `mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022` using `Dockerfile` which contains the following directive:

```Dockerfile
# Document volume mount points typically mounted from Azure file shares.
VOLUME ["D:", "Z:"]
```

which causes trouble to `containerd` failing it with error like this:

```
Error: failed to create containerd container: rootpath on
  mountPath C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume3950197485\377,
  volume Z:: CreateFile C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume3950197485\377\Z::
The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect.
```

As far as I am (and @participant2 too) reading [the docs](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#volume) correctly, my usage there looks valid. It also does not cause any trouble to Docker Desktop.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create `Dockerfile` for a custom image based on `mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022`
3. To `Dockerfile` add `VOLUME ["D:", "Z:"]` or perhaps even `VOLUME ["D:"]` is enough, I haven't tested that one.
4. Build the image e.g. `myimage` and push to remote registry
5. Deploy pod based on `myimage` to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) with. For example:

      ```yaml
      ---
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        labels:
          app: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
        name: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
      spec:
        replicas: 1
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            app: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
        template:
          metadata:
            labels:
              app: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
            name: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              kubernetes.io/os: windows
            containers:
              - name: ctr-bug6589-pv-on-d
                image: mycr.azurecr.io/myimage:latest
                command:
                - "powershell.exe"
                - "-Command"
                - "while (1) { Write-Host $(Get-Date -Format u); Add-Content -Encoding Ascii D:\\data.txt $(Get-Date -Format u); sleep 5 }"
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: pv-on-d
                    mountPath: "D:"
            volumes:
              - name: pv-on-d
                persistentVolumeClaim:
                  claimName: test-bug6589-pv-on-d-pvc
      ---
      kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
      apiVersion: v1
      metadata:
        name: test-bug6589-pv-on-d-pvc
      spec:
        accessModes:
          - ReadWriteMany
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: 2Gi
        storageClassName: azurefile-csi
      ```


### Describe the results you received and expected

The results I received were errors in the detailed AKS events for (failed) deployment of my pod:

```
Error: failed to create containerd container: rootpath on mountPath C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume3950197485\377, volume Z:: CreateFile C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume3950197485\377\Z:: The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect.
Error: failed to create containerd container: rootpath on mountPath C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume427796215\376, volume D:: CreateFile C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume427796215\376\D:: The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect.
Error: failed to create containerd container: rootpath on mountPath C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume2161075262\375, volume Z:: CreateFile C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume2161075262\375\Z:: The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect.
Error: failed to create containerd container: rootpath on mountPath C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume554088254\374, volume Z:: CreateFile C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume554088254\374\Z:: The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect.
```

The expected result was to get the pod up and running.

For example, if I replace my custom image with vanilla like below, then my pod is deployed and volume successfully mounted as `D:` drive:

```yaml
---
# File pod-mount-pv-on-d.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
  name: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
      name: test-bug6589-pv-on-d
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/os: windows
      containers:
        - name: ctr-bug6589-pv-on-d
          image: mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022
          command:
          - "powershell.exe"
          - "-Command"
          - "while (1) { Write-Host $(Get-Date -Format u); Add-Content -Encoding Ascii D:\\data.txt $(Get-Date -Format u); sleep 5 }"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: pv-on-d
              mountPath: "D:"
      volumes:
        - name: pv-on-d
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: test-bug6589-pv-on-d-pvc
---
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: test-bug6589-pv-on-d-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 2Gi
  storageClassName: azurefile-csi
```

### What version of containerd are you using?

1.6.14

### Any other relevant information

AKS with Kubernetes 1.25.5 with containerd and Windows Server 2022 node

There is very relevant comment posted by @participant2 here https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/6589#issuecomment-1429537700 as follow-up to mine linked earlier.

### Show configuration if it is related to CRI plugin.

_No response_

comments.body:
Copying over my comment from #6589:

----

Interesting. That might be a separate containerd bug to file then, as by my reading of [the docs](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#volume) your usage there looks valid.

Tracking down the error message, `rootpath on mountPath C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume3950197485\377, volume Z:` is coming from [thie code block](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/pkg/cri/opts/container.go#L120-L125), and I'm pretty sure that the bug lives here. [`fs.rootPath`](https://github.com/containerd/continuity/blob/main/fs/path.go#L223-L225) is going to try to return `C:\Windows\TEMP\ctd-volume3950197485\377` + `\` + `Z:`, but that's not a valid path on Windows. The error we're seeing is part of `fs.rootPath`'s symlink-protection checks trying to open that file, but otherwise it would have failed with `stat volume in rootfs` when that code block tried to check if the target existed in order to copy stuff from the relevant path in the rootfs into the new volume mount, in case no mount request for this path was provided in the container-launch data.

I _suspect_ this code block should simply skip drive-letter volumes other than `C:`, since I don't believe (but could be wrong) that you can store non-C: volumes in a WCOW container image; the image filesystem (`rootfs` here) is assumed to be mounted at `C:`, other drive letters are runtime-only. (I also suspect that `VOLUME ["D:", "Z:"]` also won't guarantee those drive letters exist, as they would for non-drive-letter paths, but I haven't checked that, don't know if Docker does the same thing, and that would be a _different_ bug (or feature request...) either way. #5671 went more into this area.)

I suspect the repro commands from #5671 or similar, but with a trivial Dockerfile with a `VOLUME ["D:", "Z:"]` line (which doesn't apply to Linux) would reproduce this issue with only `containerd` and `crictl`, if it helps, since that avoids the need for k8s in the repro.

To be clear, that was mostly guess-work based on looking at _just this block of code_, and it's possible I'm misreading it. We'll see what happens in the relevant bug-report discussion.

comments.body:
Having a stab at this. Hopefully I understood the issue correctly :smile:.

There are two things to discuss here:

  * How Dockerfile defined ```VOLUME``` is treated
  * How to accomplish what you need

## The ```VOLUME``` stanza

To my knowledge, volumes outside of ```C:\``` are not supported on Windows. Docker even has a function which checks if the drive letter is anything other than ```C:\```, erring out if not.

On Windows, when creating a container from an image with the ```VOLUME``` stanza, the spec gets inspected and a new volume is created. The new volume is actually a path on the host to a folder. The contents of the folder inside the image which is declared as a VOLUME (if it exists) is copied over to the newly created volume. That volume then gets mounted inside the running container.

When creating containers from such images via the ```CRI``` API (which is what k8s does), the root for the created volumes is typically in: ```C:\ProgramData\containerd\root\io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri\containers\CONTAINER_ID\volumes\VOLUME_ID\_data```. When creating containers  via nerdctl, the volumes get created in ```C:\ProgramData\nerdctl\052055e3\volumes\default\VOLUME_ID\_data```.

The error you're seeing is due to the fact that containerd doesn't expect a volume outside of ```C:\```, and doesn't think that it contains a drive letter. The check is too simplistic and will have to be fixed.

## Making arbitrary paths available in containers

What you're probably trying to do is to make those drive letters available in the running container. In ```containerd``` terms, that is normally done using a mount. 

You will most likely need to mount a folder from those drive letters, not the drive letter itself. The destination in the container will have to be a folder under ```C:\```. Something like mounting ```D:\``` on ```C:\drives\d```.

To achieve what you need, you can probably use ```hostPath``` in your yaml. Something like:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hostpath-volume-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: my-hostpath-volume-pod
    image: mycr.azurecr.io/myimage:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: foo
      mountPath: "C:\\drives\\D"
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/os: windows
  volumes:
  - name: foo
    hostPath:
     path: "D:\\myFolder"
```

Which should mount ```D:\myFolder``` from the host on ```C:\drives\D``` in the containers. I haven't tested this, but in theory, it should work.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I think you've got an underlying mistake here. [Volumes other than `C:` are supported in Windows containers as volume mount-points](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/run/#volume) (and hence [the `VOLUME` statement](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#notes-about-specifying-volumes)), there's just no (current) way to have any contents for them in an image, so they're _only_ ever volume mount points. (I'm also not sure which code in Docker you're referring to, I guess it's code related to image extraction or creation, not runtime volume mounts)

So `VOLUME ["D:"]` is valid, and should have all the effects of `VOLUME ["C:\somemount"]` or `VOLUME ["/some/mount"]` on Linux (per the docs and skimming relevant moby and containerd-cri code... I didn't check ctr though):
* Creates a mount-point (a directory) at that path at execution time.
  *  The docs don't specific execution time for this Implementations seem to be that way though, and neither [BuildKit](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/blob/3187d2d056de7e3f976ef62cd548499dc3472a7e/frontend/dockerfile/dockerfile2llb/convert.go#L1331-L1342) nor [legacy Dockerfile builder](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/2fa8f54d0869511f88efd318f67fe1d06915e78a/builder/dockerfile/dispatchers.go#L543-L557) do anything with `VOLUME` except update image metadata.
  * In practical terms, neither implementation I looked at does this on Windows or Linux, because it's implicitly done by mounting something there in the next effect.
* At execution time, if nothing is mounted there:
  * Create a temporary volume
  * Prepopulate the volume with what was in the image at that path, if anything.
  * Mount the temporary volume at the named mount-point (in read-write mode).

Because the image cannot container anything outside `C:`, that last point can never happen with `VOLUME ["D:"]`.

Also, [Docker's implementation skips this step for _all Windows volume mounts_ due to what I assume is a HCS v1 limitation](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/daemon/create_windows.go#L42-L70), since containerd-cri _does_ implement this on Windows, so the container image described in that last link would probably execute differently in Docker and containerd-cri: Both will create the temporary volume and mount it there, but on Docker it'll be empty.

Okay, I looked, and ctr doesn't appear to handle `VOLUME` at all, i.e. there's no equivalent I can immediately see for [the containerd-cri implementation](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbb2d08af077c1d298e0f7c7ae8db4f5ced85389/pkg/cri/server/container_create.go#L144-L145), so it won't even create the temporary volumes on Windows _or_ Linux.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
There is confusion in regards to what the ```VOLUME``` stanza in a ```Dockerfile``` is supposed to do and what a ```volume``` means for containerd/Docker.

The ```VOLUME``` stanza is a way of saying: "I want this folder(s) inside the container to be a folder/volume from the host, mounted at this location(s)". So when we say:

```Dockerfile
VOLUME ["C:/test", "C:/test2"]
```

We are actually saying: "please mount a volume at these locations in the container". That stanza does not say "make C:/test from the host, available inside the container". This bit of docs: https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/run/#volume is what the ```hostPath``` example I gave is supposed to do. It says: "please mount this path from the host, to this destination in the container". It basically creates a ```mount.Mount{}``` object with source and destination. The ```VOLUME``` stanza does this too, but **after** it creates a volume in the form of a folder in ```C:\ProgramData\containerd\root\io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri\containers\CONTAINER_ID\volumes\VOLUME_ID\_data```. It then mounts that in ```C:/test``` (or whatever is defined in the ```VOLUME``` stanza).

> I'm also not sure which code in Docker you're referring to, I guess it's code related to image extraction or creation, not runtime volume mounts

The code in moby I'm referring to is this: https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/pkg/archive/path_windows.go#L11. 

Here is the relevant test for containerd that ensures the contents of a ```VOLUME``` is made available in the newly created volume after a container is created: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/integration/volume_copy_up_test.go#L39. It uses ```ghcr.io/containerd/volume-copy-up:2.1``` which is defined here: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/integration/images/volume-copy-up/Dockerfile_windows#L37.

The ```VOLUME``` stanza will never make a ```D:\``` available inside a container. At least not that I am aware of. HCS would need to know how to map a folder from the host, inside a potential ```D:``` dos drive inside the container, something I am not sure is possible, 

You can mount D:\ from the host inside a container, but not via the ```VOLUME``` stanza in a ```Dockerfile```. You can do this via the command line or API by crafting a ```mount.Mount{}```.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> The `VOLUME` stanza will never make a `D:\` available inside a container. At least not that I am aware of. HCS would need to know how to map a folder from the host, inside a potential `D:` dos drive inside the container, something I am not sure is possible,

This is your underlying oversight. HCS _does_ support this and always has. Your docs-link has an example of it:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/138397/229868048-de543a25-b87c-4f23-8581-8f2dd069ca22.png)

Also note that in this bug, the repro case _works_ if you remove the `VOLUME` command from the Dockerfile, with `D:` appearing as expected in the container mounted from the requested PVC.

Edit: I just realised, that `VOLUME ["D:"]` would probably work in this repro-case, because [the code that calls this](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbb2d08af077c1d298e0f7c7ae8db4f5ced85389/pkg/cri/server/container_create.go#L201-L207) has already had any `VOLUME`-declared mount-points filtered out if [they have a mount requested by CRI](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbb2d08af077c1d298e0f7c7ae8db4f5ced85389/pkg/cri/server/container_create.go#L319-L325).

So the repro case requires that `VOLUME` refer to a drive-letter that does _not_ have a volume mounted there in the CRI request. So the repro is actually `VOLUME ["Z:"]` here. ^_^

----

The moby code you linked is used in the archiver, for creating and extracting container images, not at runtime. That's related to what I was saying about it not being possible to populate D: _in the image_, but you can definitely `VOLUME ["D:"]` to tell the runtime to populate it (with an empty volume) even if you don't mount a volume there.

(It's very possible that the genesis of `VOLUME` was that they intended to _only_ allow mounting things at declared mount-points, but I've never seen a claim to that effect, nor any environment that would have made that necessary)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
#8043 touches the exact lines you linked to in `pkg/cri/opts/container.go`. They aren't semantically changed, but it was more a warning for someone who may not be aware of #8043 that those lines would be changing a bit (basically dropping the Windows-specific code-path, which changed the indentation of the block as well).

And see https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/8171#issuecomment-1452811643, stripping the drive letters is wrong, because a container with `VOLUME ["D:"]` executed without any volume mounts must still create a temporary volume and mount it to `D:` at runtime, and `VOLUME ["D:","Z:]` needs to produce _two distinct volume mounts_, so you still need a directory for each entry in `VOLUME`. So the drive letters need to be mangled into being disk-safe for the host path, including `C:`, and perhaps _prepending_ `C:` for volumes without a drive letter.

I actually kind-of prefer the Docker implementation, which [generates a random ID for each backing volume](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/2fa8f54d0869511f88efd318f67fe1d06915e78a/volume/mounts/windows_parser.go#L383-L384), rather than trying to append the full path to the container's bundle path, which has potential path-length issues as well.

I was thinking of stripping the drive letter to see if we're left with an empty string. Any non-C drive cannot have be a sub-folder it seems, or you get:

```powershell
PS C:\var> docker run --rm -it -v C:\var\aa:D:\ ghcr.io/containerd/volume-copy-up:2.1
```

I was not suggesting that we mutate anything in ```volumeMounts``` or the runtime spec. Just check whether it's a ```C:``` or a non ```C:``` volume and skip trying to copy contents for non ```C:```.

If I am reading that bit of code correctly, the ```volumeMounts``` is a ```map[string]string{}``` of host paths to container paths. The host paths should already be created or they should already exist. The only thing that remains is to validate the container path, and skip trying to populate it if it's anything other than ```C:```.

comments.body:
Yeah, sorry, I had a brain-fart about this (and it's not the first time I've made this mistake in this ticket >\_<): The stripped path is being appended to the _source_, not the _destination_ of the copy. The _destination_ of the copy is the _source_ of the mount, which is why I keep getting this wrong. >\_< The host directories do have an appropriate random ID-based name, so yeah, just skipping volumes that start with a drive-letter other than C: is fine. And I think I knew that the first time I looked at this, based on my original comment.

I had to track this down (and am now going to go to bed before I can introduce more mistakes): [The code that names the host directories explicitly does not create their directories](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbb2d08af077c1d298e0f7c7ae8db4f5ced85389/pkg/cri/server/container_create.go#L326-L333), they're created as a very deep side-effect of [this call](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbb2d08af077c1d298e0f7c7ae8db4f5ced85389/pkg/cri/server/container_create.go#L159-L160), which also does that for explicit host-mounts of non-existent directories. (Which is a little awkward... A CRI host-path mount equivalent to `--mount src=C:\tmep,dest=D:` will actually create `C:\tmep` rather than complain that you spelled the host path wrong. Fun! I vaguely recall using this behaviour in Docker, so at least it's consistent...)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> So it seems that this is intended behavior when running with an unprivileged user

That's reminded me that this is solved for k8s mounts by `fsGroup` on Linux, and Windows has no equivalent (as k8s has no support for groups on Windows at all). But that doesn't apply to these mounts, since they're not k8s-visible.

So this issue isn't actually AKS-specific; for the image-populated `C:\test_dir`, we're probably missing copying-over of the ACLs in `copyExistingContents` (so it would need a split Windows implementation or Windows-specific code-path), and for cases where we don't call that, the default-created directory probably needs ACLs to allow non-Administrator accounts to _read_ it? It gets a bit useless in that case though, since I don't think an initContainer can be used to change the permissions as a workaround for lack of `fsGroup`, like it can for a PVC or something, so it's going to be permanently empty and read-only.

(Edit: `fs.CopyDir` _should_ be copying ACLs, assuming I'm skimming continuity correctly. Without the `VOLUME`, is C:\test_dir readable by non-Adminitrator user? Anyway, seems like it's not as simple as "copy ACLs"...)

That makes me suspect that a `VOLUME ["/doesnotexist"]` on Linux will also be read-only to a non-privileged user too. Both [Linux](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbb2d08af077c1d298e0f7c7ae8db4f5ced85389/pkg/cri/opts/spec_linux_opts.go#L113C35-L115) and [Windows](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/cbb2d08af077c1d298e0f7c7ae8db4f5ced85389/pkg/cri/opts/spec_windows_opts.go#L65-L67) create the mount-points as `0755`. Clearly that's not sufficient to allow in-container ContainerUser to read the directory though; happily that's already in a Windows-specific code-path. so a fix would be isolated.

Anyway, I think fixing this part (non-privileged user behaviour) is probably beyond scope of this issue, since the fix for _this_ issue is so simple, and resolves a "container failed to start" bug. (Same thought applies to `ctr` just completely not supporting the `VOLUME` statement here; no one's noticed this even in Linux, so it's a very low-value improvement).

Straying from topic, this magic image-volume mildly concerns me in k8s anyway, simply because it's less (or not) visible to tooling; when the directory is not populated from the image, mounting an emptydir over it will fix a bunch of issues, but I don't know how to make this work when it _is_ populating from the image (either for image-default-mutable-config reasons, or to get a prepopulated read-write mount inside a read-only-root), apart from an emptydir plus an initContainer to populate it, perhaps.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> So this issue isn't actually AKS-specific

Nope. This happens everywhere.

> for the image-populated `C:\test_dir`, we're probably missing copying-over of the ACLs in `copyExistingContents`

[fs.CopyDir()](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/pkg/cri/opts/container.go#L152) does [copy DACLs](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/vendor/github.com/containerd/continuity/fs/copy_windows.go#L33-L75), but in the case of the image I am using, the owner of ```test_dir``` apparently was inherited from ```C:\```. If I change it to ```C:\nested\test_dir```, when creating it here: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/integration/images/volume-copy-up/Dockerfile_windows#L32, the owner is correctly set to the ```ContainerUser``` SID. [The test file](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/integration/images/volume-copy-up/Dockerfile_windows#L34) has the correct owner, but we can't access it because we can't enter the parent folder.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/903160/230047429-e6923331-a58a-448e-8fed-8b2042088503.png)

So at least for volumes in ```C:\``` we can have proper ownership if we craft the Dockerfile to avoid creating them directly in ```C:\```, or at least to explicitly take ownership after it gets created.

For non ```C:\``` volumes however, there is no easy way to have them be owned by non ```Administrator``` users, as there is nothing to copy DACLs from.
